_about: Everything this build made up, one line each, PROPOSED to Griz's ear (spec §8). Nothing here is written back to the wiki. RULED 09-24 (Griz, playtest fold): the game shows no [GRIZ] stubs and does not defer key NPCs' words to him; the seat drafts them, they stand as approved, and the wiki is not edited to match gameplay.

entries.what: Barley's threshing flail statted as 1d10 bludgeoning, two-handed (so Great Weapon Fighting applies).
entries.why: No stats anywhere in the register; the register calls it 'a two-handed farm tool'.

entries.what: Barley starts with the flail and no armor (AC 11).
entries.why: The register has him owning nothing on Day -15; the game starts him at fighter 2 with his method in hand.

entries.what: The Warrens' 'Crawler' is an original stat block (AC 12, HP 40, feelers +5 1d6+2 poison with the register's CON DC 13 paralysis, mandibles +4 2d4+2).
entries.why: The carrion crawler is not in SRD 5.1; the spec forbids non-SRD monsters by name. The CON 13 touch is the register's own.

entries.what: The Stair's Keeper is an original stat block (AC 13, HP 58, constrict + drag under, STR DC 13 grapple, invisible in its water until light shows it).
entries.why: The water weird is not in SRD 5.1. The register's DC 13 and 'cannot leave its water' are kept.

entries.what: A 'Glory-Seeker' gnoll leader (CR 1, HP 38, spear + bite).
entries.why: The gnoll pack lord is not SRD; the register's Snoot overlay has glory-seekers.

entries.what: Hire terms: Barley joins if you front his 5-silver stake at the Hex; Aurdin if you cover his debt (20 sp, creditor unnamed — held OPEN); Vivian after you buy one of her candles (1 sp) and ask; Lymen once the party has any renown. Spots: Barley at the Hex bar, Lymen at the Hex, Aurdin outside the mission chapel, Vivian on vice row.
entries.why: The register gives no joining price for any of them; spots follow where the register places each.

entries.what: Hires join at the higher of their sheet level and (the lead's level - 1).
entries.why: Spec §13.7 suggestion (join-level floor).

entries.what: Level-up picks: Barley Champion at 3, STR+2 at 4; Aurdin Evocation, learns Scorching Ray + Mage Armor (3), Web + Shatter (4), Fireball + Lightning Bolt (5), INT+1/CON+1 at 4; Lymen Oath of Devotion at 3 (+Divine Favor), Heroism at 4, Lesser Restoration + Aid at 5, STR+1/CHA+1 at 4; Vivian DEX+2 at 4.
entries.why: SRD 5.1 offers one subclass per class; the register leaves Barley's and Lymen's unruled. Spells chosen from the SRD list for usefulness in menu combat (Griz 09-23: the build picks casters' spells; no need to include every spell).

entries.what: At rogue 3 the player chooses Vivian's archetype: THIEF (SRD Fast Hands: ITEM is a bonus action) or CUTTHROAT (see #cutthroat).
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz): storywise it has a lean, but in this game it's the player's choice.

entries.what: CUTTHROAT, an archetype original to this game: Opening Cut, first round only, advantage against a foe that hasn't acted yet, and a hit on it is a critical.
entries.why: The canon lean is Assassin, which is not in SRD 5.1; this is the game's own path in that direction, named and built fresh.

entries.what: Vivian's SKILL menu offers HIDE + ATTACK and ATTACK + HIDE (the bonus-action hide before or after her attack).
entries.why: Griz 09-24; SRD Cunning Action lets the bonus action fall anywhere in the turn.

entries.what: Winters' Errands: two courier runs in town. The estate papers (Androit seals, Casper Venn values, back to Winters: 12 sp, renown +1) and Pryor's debt (Mical signs the crate off, Brennan is paid, back to Winters: 20 sp and a potion, renown +1). 'The Pryor estate' is invented.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz): easy 'help people in town' renown, courier missions between important NPCs, Winters starts. Gives a solo lead early renown (and Lymen's hire).

entries.what: Ambrose Winters' own voice and lines: 'Everything on these shelves outlived somebody. I price the somebody first.' He watches Vivian's hands. He holds the Ring of Binding for whoever can use it.
entries.why: Were reserved; RULED 09-24 the seat drafts key NPCs for this game.

entries.what: Winters sells magic items after the first errand: healing potions (incl. a Superior Potion), an Elixir of Health, the Ring of Protection, +1 dagger/maul/staff, splint.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: he should sell magic items, acquisitions). Stock and gating are the game's.

entries.what: Mama's Pharmakaiea is a shop: Lucia sells simples, potions, antitoxin and kits, potions a little under the pawnbroker's price. Lucia's lines are drafted.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: make Mama's a shop).

entries.what: Hessle's drawer holds a stiff old purse of forty gold in thirty-year-old coin and an unsigned note: FOR WHOEVER COMES BACK UP. It pays 400 sp.
entries.why: The backer was held open; RULED 09-24 the seat drafts. The note keeps the backer unnamed.

entries.what: The ending: the Waterbys keep the inn; the lantern stays on its hook unlit; next morning Doran draws from the lake in front of everyone and drinks.
entries.why: Was held open ('do not ruin it'); RULED 09-24 the seat drafts. Written to not ruin it.

entries.what: Fronting Barley's five puts him straight onto the card: a solo bout vs a 'Card Bruiser' (Bandit scaled up, HP 22). Win: he hands your five back. Lose: the five is gone; he joins anyway.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: covering his silver should go straight to a fight scene).

entries.what: A shift at the cradle is a timing game: six squeezes on a swinging mark. Green = a clean thimble (1 sp), amber = a dry pull, red = the feelers (CON 13, the draught gives advantage; a fail ends the shift). Animal Handling/Nature widens the green.
entries.why: Playtest 09-24 went looking for a milking minigame. The dose-rate, six draws and CON 13 are the register's.

entries.what: JOURNAL: pin one quest; a gold arrow marks the next person, door or place it needs (or the way there from another map). Each quest carries steps with a NEXT line.
entries.why: Griz 09-24: highlight a journal entry to make it active, with a marker over whoever you need next.

entries.what: Silverton has a north gate: a cut up through the mountain's skirt, onto the Doors road. The town icon lets you in by whichever gate you walked up to.
entries.why: Playtest 09-24: no way north of town, and the Doors road was unreachable.

entries.what: Cassia's inn: 8 sp alone, a flat 16 sp for a company.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz).

entries.what: The first night the party stays at the Halfway Inn, Amara's wagon comes in (a cutscene). Whoever had second watch rolls Perception (DC 15 at the window); a success shows the children through the glamour, with no words. INVESTIGATE sends the watcher out, WAKE THE PARTY sends everyone, KEEP WATCH lets it happen. Outside: Perception DC 12 each; if still hidden, the inn lady's lie (the mine across the lake), Insight DC 13 on it, then Perception again at +5.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz's shape of the scene); the cast and the glamour are module-halfway-inn.md.

entries.what: Never seen through: the handover and the walk, with a goblin at the inn lady's side. Seen through with Lymen outside: his line, then the fight. Otherwise: 'Those are children', Amara offers 500 sp. Taken: the inn lady 'adopts' the child, the wagon leaves that night with Katarina, the child still goes to the lake, and Elsbeth never speaks to you again. Refused: the fight.
entries.why: RULED 09-24.

entries.what: Amara (AC 13, HP 38, two Eldritch Blast beams) and Willem Glass (AC 12, HP 30, Ray of Frost, Mirror Image) fight only to get away: each round one covers while the other runs for the horses (d20+DEX vs 10 + the party's best DEX, the party's own RUN rule). Amara's darkness goes up on her first run and the two drivers scatter. A lone watcher fights round one alone; the rest of the party arrives in round two.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz); stat blocks built from SRD 5.1 pieces for the module's warlock 5 and wizard 5.

entries.what: If they get to the horses: the party runs them down once on the road past the gulch (a second fight, the whole party). If they get away again, it's a chase on the world map at your own speed. The pair pulls up at the fork for about a second, and if Willem is alive he throws a false pair of riders down the west road. Catch them for a fight to the death, or they ride into the Tower, which then gives the expansion popup (its door still doesn't open).
entries.why: RULED 09-24; the false riders are module-halfway-inn.md §4 (Willem's favorite trick).

entries.what: Stopping the wagon: +1 renown; the strongbox (600 sp and Amara's order, sealed with a dove and signed V, which Hessle pays true word for, unlisted). Killed in the yard: Doran takes the wagon of children back to Newland that night. Either way, next visit: Doran gone, one girl kept back by the inn lady out back, and Elsbeth gives you the lake's thanks (+1 armor of the main's kind, or a Ring of Protection) and urges you to Winters. A later night with the ring on: the kept girl is the one who walks to the lake.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz); 'the lake gave it back' is module-halfway-inn.md §9 (bog-grave goods).

entries.what: The day after the wagon (if she didn't ride out with it), Katarina gives the party her book and walks south; if she did ride out, it's in the drawer upstairs. READ shows the opening of Book One (serial-castegut installment 01, to 'Now the first thing.'). Given to Androit: +2 renown, not in the journal.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz).

entries.what: After the credits, CONTINUE: morning at the lake. The inn lady sits inconsolable at the table; Doran thanks you, says he lost his way, and gives you free rooms for good; Elsbeth sells candles on vice row in Silverton.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz).

entries.what: The listed true word is the Snoot. Beating the Snoot's challenge on the road yields a Dominion wagoneer's anchor-pin taken at the moot; Hessle pays 500 sp for it.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (the listed true word is re: the Snoot; a drop the party takes to claim it).

entries.what: Spell-component parts from monsters, if someone standing has the skill (no roll): bat fur and wings (Survival), gulch silk from spiders and the ettercap (Survival or Nature), darkmantle hide (Survival), crawler ichor (Arcana), glow glands from fire beetles, snake tongues (Survival or Nature), axe beak feathers and wolf fur (Survival). Only Percy buys them, at a fifth of the rendered price. Bat wings he won't take; Marta Venn cooks them into bat-wing pies (1 sp each, free with Vivian in the party): eaten in a fight, +2 CON and +5 HP until it ends.
entries.why: RULED 09-24 (Griz: parts, a fifth of post-process pricing; wings to Viv's mom).

entries.what: Percy's Particulars has an interior: jars in ranks, Percy at the counter, Ned Halloway minding the shelves, the shelf card on the wall (flavor, nothing for sale).
entries.why: Griz 09-24; the shelf is shops-silverton.json pin 38.

entries.what: Dancing Lights can be cast in battle: dim light, but it reveals anything unseen (the Keeper in its water). It doesn't dazzle, and it's not fire.
entries.why: Playtest 09-24 asked whether the out-of-combat light should help in a fight. SRD Dancing Lights is dim light; the reveal is the game's.

entries.what: Find Familiar is cut from Aurdin's book.
entries.why: Griz 09-24: no reason it should be in the game.

entries.what: Lymen's AC is computed as 19 (chain mail 16 + shield 2 + Defense 1).
entries.why: His sheet reads 18 with Defense 'included' — the arithmetic doesn't reach 18. Flagged for Griz.

entries.what: Currency is silver pieces; SRD gp prices x10. Register prices win where they exist.
entries.why: The town talks in silver; the Hex stake, the dose-rate and the lantern law are all in silver.

entries.what: Calla's 'simples' heal 1d4+2 in the game.
entries.why: The register prices theriac/purges/simples at ~2 sp but gives no effect.

entries.what: A healer's kit is sold per use (5 sp) and gets a KO'd hero up at 1 HP.
entries.why: SRD kit (10 uses for 5 gp) stabilizes; the spec wants KO'd heroes revived 'with an item'.

entries.what: The tent is a consumable short-rest item (half HP back; Second Wind, Action Surge, Channel Divinity recover).
entries.why: Spec §7: short rest = a TENT item.

entries.what: Warding chalk pushes the next random encounter back ~60 steps.
entries.why: The register sells warding chalk and threshold lines with 'no promises made'; the effect is the game's.

entries.what: Lisbet's charm is a ring-slot item with no effect.
entries.why: 'Charms (no promises made)' — taken at its word.

entries.what: Vilar's show-armorer sells the full SRD weapon and armor list (beyond the register's spear, mace, shield); Kessler's pawn stocks a few pledges (rapier, crossbow, studded, splint, potion, two +1 weapons).
entries.why: The register has no armorer; Lymen's chain mail came from the show-armorer, so the game treats Vilar's as the armor shop.

entries.what: A night at the Halfway Inn costs 5 sp a head.
entries.why: No price in the register for ordinary guests.

entries.what: Encounter weights, group sizes and step rates for every zone.
entries.why: The register's road d20 and regional d8s name the creatures; the numbers are the game's.

entries.what: The Hex ladder for a free fighter: a floor-bet brawl (Bandit stats, fists), a freeman challenge vs a stable fighter (Thug), the card vs a hired blade (Bandit Captain stats), Talmok (register block, pit fists), then a festival bout (Berserker). Bouts are solo; a loser is stitched up on the house at 1 HP.
entries.why: The register has no ladder for free fighters; the rungs follow its stated rules.

entries.what: Under a roosted ceiling, fire and thunder spells are grayed out in MAGIC (marked ROOST). Casting Light, lighting a torch, or throwing an oil flask brings the roof down: the bats fill the screen and the run ends in a failure screen, NOT THIS KIND OF NAME. Every roost battle opens with a one-line reminder (no fire, no bright light).
entries.why: The register's one law (no fire, no noise; hooded lamps only). RULED 09-24 (Griz): a 'you wanted to make a name for yourself, but not this kind of name' failure; gray out the spells, keep Light or a torch as the trigger.

entries.what: Warrens flow: talk to Edric (or work a shift) to get in the book; talk to Skarn 'as a man' to open his gate; take the bucket to feed the otyugh or fight it; the mark wakes the keeper; rope the five out from the landing or wade in and fight. Killing 6+ crawlers makes the stock 'dead' and Dunmore's line holds the camp.
entries.why: Every step is the register's; the thresholds and the order are the game's.

entries.what: The rescue set-piece is fixed in G3's side gallery (four giant bats); pits in G3 drop to G4; bad air costs 1d4 on a failed CON 12.
entries.why: The register's set-piece is a d6 table fired once on the GM's word.

entries.what: Casting Light or using a torch in battle: the first time, the cloaker recoils and loses its next turn; after that its attacks are at disadvantage (shown as DAZZLED). It also reveals the Keeper.
entries.why: SRD Light Sensitivity; the register says light is the weapon. The lost turn is the game's (playtest: the light needed to visibly do something).

entries.what: The lake's offering plays the first night the party sleeps at the Halfway Inn holding the Ring of Binding; the chuul then waits at the point.
entries.why: Griz ruled what the cutscene shows (the inn lady and the kid go, only the inn lady comes back); when it plays is the game's.

entries.what: The Castegut road ends at a signpost (not this road, not this time); the east and west edges are the sea, the cliffs and the black mountains.
entries.why: Spec §5: east/west stoppages as appropriate.

entries.what: Ettercap fangs and the cloaker's tail are the proof tokens for Hessle's board.
entries.why: The register names the tail; the fangs are the game's.

entries.what: The lead starts in the Gate Plaza with 10 silver, 3 simples and 1 healer's kit.
entries.why: Barley's ten silver is canon; the rest is the game's.

entries.what: Each major quest (Pete's five, the rescue, the cloaker, the ettercap, Talmok, the Snoot) pays a magic weapon of the hero's own kind to the main and to one hired companion in the party: +1 for the first two, +2 after. Barley's is his threshing flail made +1/+2.
entries.why: Griz 09-23, mid-build: 'add magic weapons as reward for major quest - one for main and one for one hired'. The weapons are SRD Weapon +1/+2.

entries.what: Narration and UI lines marked 'invented: connective' in content/text.json and content/npcs.json.
entries.why: Glue between register facts.

entries.what: A Renown counter (+1 per resolved local job, +2 for the lake) and its titles; each point also gives 250 milestone XP to everyone standing.
entries.why: Spec §4: 'local hero' as the motive.

entries.what: All tile maps are simplified from corridor v3, city v6, environs v3 and the module sheets; building footprints, the Hex outline and the dungeon layouts are approximate.
entries.why: 8-bit tile scale.

stubs_drafted_09_24: Vivian's roguish archetype -> the player's choice (#vivian-archetype, #cutthroat).
flagged_for_griz: Lymen's sheet says AC 18; chain mail + shield + Defense makes 19.
fighter-barley.md records 'all three leads are level 2 at campaign start' (09-01) while the spec rules Aurdin's level 2 game-only (09-23).
Show-armorer: 'Villar' in shops-silverton.json, 'Vilar' elsewhere (the game uses Vilar).
Burned voice: the wiki gives it to Falstaff, silverton-personae.md to Merrick (the game gives it to Falstaff, per the wiki).
Kessler: the wiki's pronoun is 'her'; the portrait reads as a man. The game uses no pronoun.
